messages.body_plain:
Yes -- ergm does support analysis of bipartite networks.

All of the bipartite-specific terms start with "b1..." and "b2...", and 
some of the regular terms can be used with bipartite nets also.

To get a list:

search.ergmTerms("bipartite")

Jenny

messages.body_plain:
Dear All,


I am writing to restart an old conversation from the summer. I am attempting to fit an ERGM on a directed network with 32K nodes. The network represents a needle sharing network, and the network parameters include a mix of dyadic independent and dependent terms. The target statistics for these parameters have been estimated from meta-analyses of empirical data.


Ideally, we would like to include the following terms: edges; mixing on gender, age (coded as a binary ?young? vs ?old?), and race; in- and out-degree distributions; and, a custom term we coded for distance. So, far we have had success in getting some of the simpler models to fit well, but we are running into difficulties when we try to fit a larger subset of the terms above. A summary of the models that we have tried, and a list of suggestions that we received in the last round, are below:


Suggestions


1. To fit terms sequentially one-by-one, to investigate if the problem can be diagnosed.

2. To increase the MCMC parameters to see if convergence can be obtained.

3. To check the summary netstats for all terms.

4. To share the actual output from the fitting process, including any warnings, the fit summary and the MCMC diagnostics.


I have conducted each of these steps, and the output is available at. I summarize the main conclusions below:


Summary of model fits


  *   Preamble: Contains estimation of the target statistics for the parameters: (Link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.tlulkhm2f9ss>)


  *   A dyadic independent model: edges+nodemix(?gender?, base=1)+nodemix(?young, base=1) converges (Link).<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.u5gx59zccctz>


  *   If race mixing is added to Model 0 above, of the form ?+ nodemix("race.num", base=1), ?, san.maxit=100)? the diagnostics on some terms are good, and others look off. (Link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.far7p4qkollq>)


  *   If edges and a nodemix on race are the only terms estimated (leaving out ?gender? and?young?), the fits looks pretty good (and I suspect the fit could be improved further with further increasing san or MCMC parameters). (Link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.8aodbt397hcb>)


  *   If edges, idegree, and odegree are included together, the MCMC diagnostics look poor (Link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.bjqitasvo6ib>).The edges+idegree (link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.rksksl8vw96d>) and the edges+odegree (link<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16NzSIrIDhWZWqqEnRKv2VURSazpDjByG2GePwMJgiIs/edit#bookmark=id.nggofvia71re>) models fit much better, however.


We are looking for any ideas on how to incorporate both in- and out-degree distributions, and as large a subset of the parameters as can be incorporated. Any suggestions are most appreciated.


Many thanks.


Sincerely,

Aditya



?On 8/14/19, 12:05 PM, "martina morris" <morrism@uw.edu> wrote:



    Hi Aditya,



    We're estimating with popsizes of 50K, so it can be done.  We've learned a

    bit about how to diagnose issues.



    If you haven't already done this,



    1. i'm a bit worried about the nodemix + edges + nodematch getting close

    to (or actually being) overparameterized.  so think through whether you

    have the degrees of freedom for this specification.



    assuming that's ok...



    2. check the summary netstats for all terms, to make sure there are not

    problems.



    3. as SMG suggests, add one term at a time to see if you can isolate the

    problem.



    4. look at the mcmc.diagnostics, to make sure the models have converged

    properly.  esp. if you have some small grps in this large popn, you may

    need to use much larger intervals to get convergence.



    5. when you send us output, we need to see the actual output from the

    fitting process -- any warnings etc.  and the fit summary (i.e.:

    summary(fitobject).  and it helps alot to see the mcmc.diagnostics.



    best,

    mm

messages.body_plain:
Yes, of course.  EpiModel is designed to work with egocentrically sampled 
data, but that only influences the fitting process.

with egocentric data: initialize net, define target stats explicitly, fit
with complete nets: calculate target stats with "summary", fit

Example below.  HTH

# network
data("faux.mesa.high")

# Define the formation model
formation <- ~ edges + nodefactor("Race") + nodematch("Race", diff=T)

# Input the appropriate target statistics for each term
target.stats <- summary(faux.mesa.high ~ edges +
                           nodefactor("Race") +
                           nodematch("Race", diff=T))

# Parameterize the dissolution model
coef.diss <- dissolution_coefs(dissolution = ~offset(edges), duration = 
50)
coef.diss

# Review the arguments for the netest function
args(netest)

# Fit the model
est <- netest(faux.mesa.high, formation, target.stats, coef.diss)

# Model diagnostics
dx <- netdx(est, nsims = 10, nsteps = 1000,
             nwstats.formula = ~edges + nodefactor("Race") +
               nodematch("Race", diff=T) + degree(0:4))
dx

# Plot the formation diagnostics
plot(dx)

nwstats1 <- get_nwstats(dx, sim = 1)
head(nwstats1, 20)

# Plot the dissolution diagnostics
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3,3,2,1))
plot(dx, type = "duration", mean.col = "black")
plot(dx, type = "dissolution", qnts = 0.5,
      mean.lines = FALSE, sim.lines = FALSE)

# Static (cross-sectional ERGM) model diagnostics (if the dynamic dx are 
not looking good)
dx.static <- netdx(est, nsims = 10000, dynamic = FALSE)
dx.static

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
plot(dx.static, sim.lines = TRUE, sim.lwd = 0.1)

nwstats2 <- get_nwstats(dx.static)
head(nwstats2, 20)
